analysis: The only change is at BackendParityHarness.swift line 435 (loadDrafter): `Gemma4AssistantDraftModel.load(from:)` becomes `MLXLLM.Gemma4AssistantDraftModel.load(from:)`. This is a module-qualification change that disambiguates the type name. It adds no new inputs, I/O or trust-boundary crossings, and it does not touch the crypto, attestation, authorization, prefix-cache, or coordinator-facing code paths. The harness lives in the ProviderBenchmark target. It is a developer and benchmark tool that loads local model directories, builds engines through EngineV2Factory.makeProductionBuild with constructionPurpose .benchmark, and uses a PrefixCacheV2 in-memory cache scoped "g2-parity". It does not use the production SSD cache tier, so T-041 is not affected. The remaining unverified contract is whether the qualified `MLXLLM.Gemma4AssistantDraftModel` resolves to the same implementation as before. That depends on whether a same-named type exists in another imported module, such as ProviderCore, and on which type Gemma4CBv2MTPDrafter expects. The supplied evidence does not show this, and it is a build-correctness and behavior question rather than a demonstrated security regression. If the qualified type differs from what was previously resolved, the drafter load path could change, but only in the benchmark harness. No finding is raised.
